story.title: The work changes. Its lineage remains.
paragraphs: Star Splitter Records is one evolving catalog directed by Jeff Hines and expressed through distinct artist projects. The projects are creative languages—not fictional biographies and not simply genre folders. Each gives the music a different voice, emotional perspective, and visual world.

A release may begin as a complete composition, an earlier recording, a new interpretation, a reconstruction, a remix, or a more generative starting point. Those beginnings are not interchangeable, and the credits do not treat them as though they are.

Release credits separate composition, lyrics, arrangement, performance, production, editing, curation, source material, and related versions whenever those distinctions matter. The purpose is neither to conceal the tools nor to make them the subject. It is to show what actually happened and preserve the lineage of the work.

licensing.title: A catalog built for many kinds of scenes.
licensing.intro: Instrumentals, alternate versions, stems, clean versions, and project-specific music support film, television, games, advertising, and other visual work. The catalog is organized around source relationships, version history, and production credits—useful context for licensing conversations.

footer.tagline: Distinct musical worlds. Clearly preserved lineage.

creditNote.title: Origin and transformation are both part of the story.
creditNote.body: Star Splitter separates composition, interpretation, performance, and production so a release can be credited for what it actually is—not reduced to a single tool, process, or category.

authorship.title: Credit the origin. Credit the transformation.
authorship.intro: Composition, interpretation, performance, and production are different forms of creative contribution. Star Splitter names them separately so listeners can understand where a work began, what changed, and who shaped the final release.

principles.title: The composition
principles.body: Who originated the melody, harmony, rhythm, lyrics, and underlying structure.

principles.title: The realization
principles.body: How the work was arranged, performed, generated, recorded, produced, edited, and selected.

principles.title: The lineage
principles.body: Which source composition, earlier recording, remix, restoration, or alternate version this release belongs to.

principles.title: The final decisions
principles.body: Who chose what remained, what changed, and when the work was finished.

authorship.closing: The result is specific rather than categorical: not a blanket label, but a record of the work itself.
